h: Exalted Guests and Guests of Faith: The Full and the Lacking Sukkah

p: בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (אֱמוֹר, זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג קג, ב):
In the holy Zohar (Emor, Zohar III 103b):
"You shall dwell in sukkos seven days" (Vayikra 23:42):
be seated, guests of faith, be seated."
are a chariot for the seven middos
וְאִיתָא (רַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא פִּנְחָס, זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רנה, ב):
And it is stated (Ra'aya Mehemna, Pinchas, Zohar III 255b):
is in the secret of the two combinations,
And so sukkah comes to that in numerical value, etc.
That is, sukkah written full is Malchus,
and it has the vav within it,
for the middah of Malchus surrounds the vav;
and this is in the secret of
as it will be in the future,
when Hakadosh Baruch Hu will make
a circle of dancers for the tzaddikim,
and He will sit among them in Gan Eden
And sukkah written lacking is Binah,
for the s'chach covers over the vav,
and it is as a surrounding light above.
dwells in the midst of Bnei Yisrael,
and there is formed the supernal sukkah, Binah,
which is the middah of Malchus within Binah,
And this is the matter of a sukkah
for it is Malchus, the tenth,
That is, when the sukkah includes all ten,
in the manner of what is said
it is stated in Ra'aya Mehemna:
for it is kaf, Keser Elyon, etc.,
and Kudsha Brich Hu answered him,
and there is no kavod without kaf, etc."
That is, sukkah is Binah, teshuvah;
and the fiftieth gate is the da'as
that was revealed to Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues
and was not revealed to Moshe Rabbeinu
knew nothing of evil at all:
when he was born the house filled with light,
"Every precious thing his eye has seen" (Iyov 28:10)
this is Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues
(as written in Midrash Rabbah and Tanchuma, Chukas,
בַּמִּדְבָּר רַבָּה יט, ו; תַּנְחוּמָא חֻקַּת ח);
things that were not revealed to Moshe
were revealed to Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues.
And this is what was said (Berachos 34b):
"In the place where baalei teshuvah stand,
completely righteous people do not stand."
That is because they draw with greater force;
and another tip, which shines to Binah
וַיִּקְרָא, זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג י, ב).
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר וְלֵית כָּבוֹד בְּלָא כ׳:
And this is what it says, "there is no kavod without kaf":
and a sukkah of twenty is valid,
only above twenty is it invalid.
And there is one who merits, even in our times,
that is, one who merits the 'supernal Shabbos,'
from this he merits the 'exalted guests,'
שֶׁהַסּוּכָּה סוֹכֵךְ גַּם עַל גַּבֵּי ו׳
for the sukkah covers also over the vav,
וְכָל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל עַל כָּל פָּנִים
And every single Jew, at the very least,
which is the middah of Malchus;
and this one merits the 'guests of faith.'
And this is what it says:
"He would raise his hands and rejoice:
as it is written, 'For Hashem's portion is His people'"
שֶׁעַל כָּל פָּנִים כָּל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל
for at the very least every single Jew
sukkah is also written lacking the vav;
everyone to merit the supernal sukkah,
a surrounding light over the vav,
like Yaakov, who merited the middah of emes,
as it is written, "The lip of truth shall be established forever"
to dwell in the shade of faith;
(רַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא פִּנְחָס, זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רל, א):
"He is emes and She is emunah";
one merits the guests of faith.

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 103b (Emor) — "Rav Hamnuna Saba, when he entered the sukkah, would rejoice and stand at the door of the sukkah inside and say: Let us invite the guests, let us set the table. And he would stand and bless and say: 'In sukkos you shall dwell seven days' — be seated, exalted guests, be seated; be seated, guests of faith, be seated."

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Sefer Baal Shem Tov, Emor — “‘In sukkos you shall dwell seven days’ (Vayikra 23:42): by the plain sense it should have said the reverse, ‘seven days you shall dwell in sukkos.’ Rather, this is its meaning: you, human beings, see that in the sukkos you seat, through your deeds, the seven supernal days, that is, the seven supernal guests, as is known.” Connection: The Baal Shem Tov reads the same verse, as the Zohar does, as the seating of the seven supernal guests through one's deeds.

paragraphs.text: Zohar Chadash, Toldos — Rosh Hashanah corresponds to Yitzchak, who was born on it, and we mention the Akeidah of Yitzchak; it is the day of judgment, corresponding to the attribute of judgment. Yom Kippur corresponds to Moshe, through whom the Holy One accepted prayer, pitied Israel and returned the Luchos. Sukkos corresponds to Aharon, in whose merit the seven Clouds went, covering Israel like sukkos; and therefore they make a sukkah.

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 255b (Ra'aya Meheimna, Pinchas) — "Sukkah written with the letter vav is in the secret of the two combinations, Havayah and Adnus, and so sukkah amounts in gematria to Yahadonahi…; 'sukkos' lacking the vav, of which it is said, 'In sukkos you shall dwell seven days,' is Imma."

paragraphs.text: Taanis 31a — "Ulla of Bira said in the name of Rabbi Elazar: In the future the Holy One, blessed be He, will make a circle dance for the righteous, and He will sit among them in Gan Eden, and each one will point with his finger, as it says, 'And it shall be said on that day: Behold, this is our God; we hoped to Him and He saved us… let us rejoice and be glad in His salvation' (Yeshayahu 25:9)."

paragraphs.text: Sotah 12a — “The Sages say: When Moshe was born, the whole house filled with light. Here it is written, She saw that he was good; and there it is written, God saw the light, that it was good.” The association of good with light is explicit in the Gemara. Rav Tzadok reads Moshe's original spiritual portion through this image of light preceding encounter with evil.

paragraphs.text: Berachos 34b — "R. Abahu said: In the place where ba'alei teshuvah stand, the completely righteous cannot stand, as it says, 'Peace, peace, to the far and to the near' — the far first, then the near." This disputes R. Yochanan, who holds the completely righteous are greater. Rashi: "the near" is one who was far from sin all his days, a tzaddik from the start.

paragraphs.text: Commentary: R. Eliyahu de Vidas, Reshis Chochmah, Sha'ar HaKedushah 14 — he cites the Zohar (Emor 103b) on Rav Hamnuna Sava inviting the “exalted guests” and saying “Fortunate is our portion,” and concludes: “Thus a person inside the sukkah is surrounded by an air of holiness… and therefore it is fitting to keep away from idle talk and jesting there, and to fulfill ‘rejoice with trembling.’” Connection: Reshis Chochmah draws on the same Zohar about Rav Hamnuna Sava and the guests of the sukkah that the maamar explains.
